notice: RN bank batch 146: Pediatric case studies: leukemia, hemophilia, iron deficiency anemia and iron poisoning, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A toddler with sickle cell disease is brought in by a parent. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely problem in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Apply cold packs to the abdomen to ease the pain
Encourage the toddler to walk to relieve pain
Give a diuretic to reduce the spleen size

rationale.correct: Sudden splenic enlargement with shock in a young child with sickle cell disease is sequestration.

perOption.c1: Sudden large spleen, falling hemoglobin and shock.
perOption.c2: Does not cause a rapidly enlarging spleen with shock.
perOption.c4: Would show a low reticulocyte count and no big spleen.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on splenic sequestration.

exhibits.title: Emergency
exhibits.body: 2-year-old, pale, lethargic. Spleen 6 cm below the rib margin (was not palpable last month). Hemoglobin 4.1 g/dL (baseline 8). HR 182/min, BP 70/40 mm Hg. Reticulocytes high.

questions.stem: For each child, choose the interpretation of the vital signs.

options.text: Dangerously slow for age; assess now

rationale.correct: Children's normal vital signs change with age; bradycardia in a child is ominous.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: On a pediatric unit, four children need the nurse. Which child should the nurse see first?

options.text: A 6-year-old with leukemia and an ANC of 300 whose temperature just rose to 38.5 C
A 10-year-old with a femur fracture in traction who rates pain 6 out of 10
A 3-year-old with gastroenteritis who has had one loose stool this shift
A 14-year-old with type 1 diabetes whose glucose before lunch is 210 mg/dL

rationale.correct: Fever with neutropenia is a time-critical emergency.

perOption.a: Febrile neutropenia can progress to sepsis within hours.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize children on a pediatric unit.

questions.stem: A pediatric nurse is working with an assistant (UAP) this shift. Which of these jobs may the nurse hand over? Select all that apply.

options.text: Weigh an infant on the same scale each morning
Record intake and output, including diaper weights
Feed a stable toddler without swallowing problems
Assess a child's pain after an opioid dose
Teach parents how to give oral iron
Decide whether a child with a fever needs a blood culture

rationale.correct: UAPs weigh, measure and feed; assessment, teaching and decisions stay with the RN.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: Factor VIII is dosed to raise the level by 50%. One unit/kg raises the level by about 2%. The child weighs 30 kg. How many units should the nurse prepare? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: Units = weight x desired rise / 2 = 30 x 50 / 2 = 750 units.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of iron deficiency anemia.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate about toddler nutrition.

rows.text: Toddlers should drink no more than about 16 to 24 ounces of milk a day
Weaning from the bottle by 12 to 15 months is advised
A heavy child cannot be anemic
Iron-rich foods include meat, beans and iron-fortified cereal

rationale.correct: Limit milk, wean the bottle and add iron-rich foods.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that show serious iron poisoning.

rationale.correct: GI bleeding, acidosis and a high iron level mean severe toxicity.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: If the child swallowed all 20 tablets (65 mg elemental iron each), what dose of elemental iron per kg was taken? The child weighs 12 kg. Record your answer in mg/kg as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 20 x 65 = 1,300 mg; 1,300 / 12 = 108 mg/kg. Above 60 mg/kg is potentially severe.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Deferoxamine 15 mg/kg/hr IV. Whole bowel irrigation. PICU.

questions.stem: During deferoxamine, the urine turns a red-orange (vin rosé) color and blood pressure falls to 76/44 mm Hg. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stop all IV fluids until the pressure recovers
Treat the urine color as a transfusion reaction

rationale.correct: Vin rosé urine is expected; hypotension needs a slower rate and fluids.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

"I won't call the iron 'candy'."
"Keeping them in my handbag is safe enough."

rationale.correct: Locked storage and Poison Control.

exhibits.title: 18-month well visit

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 2-year-old child (12 kg) swallowed an unknown number of a parent's ferrous sulfate 325 mg tablets (65 mg elemental iron each) about 2 hours ago. Up to 20 tablets are missing.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
